source_clause: An order can only be cancelled if its status is 'pending', and the user must confirm the reason for cancellation.
ambiguous_version: Agents must not cancel all pending orders without user confirmation.
unambiguous_version: Agents must not cancel any pending order without first obtaining explicit user confirmation; every cancellation requires confirmation.
ambiguity_point: 'must not ... all' — negation wide-scope: agents must not cancel any order (blanket prohibition); negation narrow-scope: agents need not cancel every order (selectivity permitted).
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (not > all): Agents are prohibited from cancelling any pending orders without confirmation — a blanket requirement for confirmation on every order.
Interpretation B (all > not): Agents are not required to cancel all pending orders without confirmation — some orders can be cancelled without confirmation, just not all of them.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent might cancel some orders unilaterally without confirmation, treating the rule as permission to skip confirmation on individual cases. Under Interpretation A the agent always requires confirmation before any cancellation.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_pending_order(order_id: string, reason: string) — Cancels an order. Returns updated order status.
annotation_rationale: Classic negation–universal quantifier scope ambiguity: 'must not cancel all' is ambiguous between NOT(∀x cancel(x)) and ∀x NOT(cancel(x) without confirmation). The two readings yield opposite behavioral prescriptions for individual cancellation events.

source_clause: The user needs to confirm the order id and the reason (either 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake') for cancellation.
ambiguous_version: Every item in a pending order may be modified once to a different product option or a different product type.
unambiguous_version: Every item in a pending order may be modified once to a different option of the same product type only; changing to a different product type is not permitted.
ambiguity_point: 'different product option or a different product type' — does 'different' scope over just 'product option' (narrow: option OR type are both valid targets) or does the disjunction compound two separately scoped alternatives?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Modification is allowed to either a different option of the same product OR to a completely different product type — cross-type modification is permitted.
Interpretation B: Modification is allowed to a different option within the same product type only; 'product type' modification is a separate (impermissible) class.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent approves a customer switching from a blue shirt to black shoes (cross-type). Under Interpretation B the agent refuses this and only allows e.g. blue shirt → red shirt.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies items in a pending order. Can only be called once per order.
annotation_rationale: Coordination ambiguity: the disjunction 'different product option or a different product type' allows two parses — one in which both alternatives are valid modification targets, and one in which only same-type option changes are valid. Different scope assignments produce categorically different permission sets.

source_clause: Before taking any action that updates the database, you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation.
ambiguous_version: You must list and confirm all action details before updating the database or transferring to a human agent.
unambiguous_version: Before updating the database, you must list all action details and obtain explicit confirmation. Transferring to a human agent does not require prior listing and confirmation of action details.
ambiguity_point: 'before updating the database or transferring to a human agent' — does 'before' scope over the full disjunction (confirmation required before either action) or only over 'updating the database'?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The confirmation requirement applies to both database updates AND transfers to a human agent — the agent must list details and confirm before transferring.
Interpretation B: The confirmation requirement applies only to database updates; transfer to a human agent can happen without prior listing and confirmation.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent delays a transfer while listing and confirming details, potentially frustrating a user who needs urgent human assistance. Under Interpretation B transfers happen immediately when warranted.
stripped_tool_desc: transfer_to_human_agents(summary: string) — Transfers the conversation to a human agent with an optional summary.
annotation_rationale: Conditional–disjunction scope ambiguity: 'before [X or Y]' is ambiguous between 'before X and before Y' (wide scope of 'before') and 'before X, or Y' (narrow scope). Two distinct behavioral prescriptions result.

source_clause: Refunds are processed via the original payment method immediately if it is a gift card, otherwise in 5 to 7 business days.
ambiguous_version: Refunds for cancelled or returned orders are processed immediately via the original payment method if it is a gift card.
unambiguous_version: Refunds for cancelled orders are processed immediately via the original payment method if it is a gift card. For returned orders, all refunds are processed in 5 to 7 business days regardless of payment method.
ambiguity_point: 'cancelled or returned orders' — does the 'immediately if gift card' condition apply to both order types (wide scope) or only to cancellations (narrow scope)?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Immediate gift-card refunds apply to both cancelled orders and returned orders — any gift card refund across both operations is immediate.
Interpretation B: Immediate gift-card refunds apply only to cancellations; returns follow a different timeline regardless of payment method.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent tells a customer returning an order that their gift card refund will be immediate. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly states a 5–7 business day timeline for returns even when the method is a gift card.
stripped_tool_desc: return_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Initiates a return for delivered order items.
annotation_rationale: Quantifier–conditional scope ambiguity: the disjunctive subject 'cancelled or returned orders' interacts with the conditional 'if it is a gift card' in a way that allows the conditional to scope over either just one or both order types.

source_clause: You can only help one user per conversation and must deny any requests for tasks related to any other user.
ambiguous_version: Agents may not assist users with orders or account changes without authenticating each request.
unambiguous_version: Agents may not assist any user with orders or account changes until that user has been authenticated at the start of the conversation. Authentication is performed once per conversation, not per request.
ambiguity_point: 'authenticating each request' — does 'each' scope such that every individual request requires re-authentication (distributive), or does authentication of the session cover all subsequent requests (collective)?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (distributive): Every individual request requires its own authentication step — the agent must re-verify the user's identity before each action.
Interpretation B (collective): A single authentication at the start of the conversation covers all requests in that session.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent repeatedly asks for email/zip verification before each tool call, creating severe friction and unusual behavior. Under Interpretation B authentication happens once and all subsequent requests proceed without re-verification.
stripped_tool_desc: find_user_id_by_email(email: string) — Looks up a user ID by email address. find_user_id_by_name_zip(first_name: string, last_name: string, zip: string) — Looks up a user ID by name and zip code.
annotation_rationale: Distributive–collective quantifier ambiguity on 'each request': the distributive reading requires per-request authentication while the collective reading treats the conversation session as the unit. These produce radically different interaction patterns.

source_clause: For a pending order, each item can be modified to an available new item of the same product but of different product option.
ambiguous_version: The agent must confirm details and payment before modifying items or payment methods in a pending order.
unambiguous_version: Before modifying items in a pending order, the agent must confirm the item details and the payment method for price differences. Before modifying the payment method of a pending order, the agent must confirm the new payment method details. Both operations require separate explicit confirmations.
ambiguity_point: 'before modifying items or payment methods' — does 'confirm details and payment' scope over both operations jointly or does each operation have its own confirmation requirements?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: A single confirmation covering both details and payment is required before either operation — the agent asks for one combined confirmation.
Interpretation B: Each operation type (item modification vs. payment modification) has its own confirmation requirement with its own relevant details to confirm.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent might present a combined confirmation for both item and payment changes even when only one is requested. Under Interpretation B the agent tailors confirmation content to the specific operation being performed.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_payment(order_id: string, payment_method_id: string) — Changes the payment method of a pending order.
annotation_rationale: Modal–disjunction scope ambiguity: the obligation 'must confirm' interacts with the disjunctive object 'items or payment methods' such that the scope of the confirmation requirement over each disjunct is unclear.

source_clause: Flight can be cancelled if any of the following is true: the booking was made within the last 24 hours, the flight was cancelled by the airline, it is a business flight, or the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered.
ambiguous_version: Agents may cancel a flight if the user has travel insurance and the booking was made within 24 hours or the flight was cancelled by the airline.
unambiguous_version: Agents may cancel a flight if: (a) the user has travel insurance AND the cancellation reason is covered by insurance, OR (b) the booking was made within 24 hours, OR (c) the flight was cancelled by the airline. Conditions (b) and (c) do not require travel insurance.
ambiguity_point: 'travel insurance and the booking was made within 24 hours or the airline cancelled' — does 'travel insurance' conjoin only with '24 hours' (narrow) or with the entire disjunction including 'airline cancelled' (wide)?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (insurance AND (24h OR airline-cancelled)): Travel insurance is required for both the 24-hour window and airline-cancellation cases.
Interpretation B ((insurance AND 24h) OR airline-cancelled): Airline cancellation is a standalone condition that does not require insurance; insurance is only relevant for the 24-hour case.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent refuses to cancel a flight that was cancelled by the airline if the user lacks travel insurance — an incorrect denial. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly processes the cancellation because airline cancellation is a standalone qualifying condition.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels a flight reservation. Does not verify cancellation eligibility.
annotation_rationale: Conjunction–disjunction scope ambiguity: 'A and B or C' is canonically ambiguous between '(A and B) or C' and 'A and (B or C)', producing structurally distinct eligibility conditions.

source_clause: Basic economy is a cabin class completely distinct from economy and cannot be modified once booked.
ambiguous_version: Passengers with basic economy tickets or bookings made more than 24 hours ago cannot modify their flights.
unambiguous_version: The following passengers cannot modify their flights: (a) any passenger holding a basic economy ticket, regardless of when the booking was made; (b) any passenger — in any cabin class — whose booking was made more than 24 hours ago.
ambiguity_point: 'basic economy tickets or bookings made more than 24 hours ago' — does 'passengers with' scope over both disjuncts (two independent conditions) or only over 'basic economy tickets' (modifier attachment to first disjunct only)?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Two independent conditions: (1) basic economy passengers cannot modify, AND (2) anyone whose booking is over 24 hours old cannot modify — regardless of cabin.
Interpretation B: A single compound condition: passengers who have basic economy tickets or have made bookings over 24 hours ago — both attributes must characterize the same passenger type.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A a non-basic-economy passenger with a booking over 24 hours old is blocked from modification. Under Interpretation B only basic-economy passengers with old bookings are blocked, allowing non-basic-economy passengers with older bookings to modify.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies the flights in a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Modifier attachment ambiguity in coordination: 'passengers with [X or Y]' allows 'with' to scope over just X or over the entire disjunction X or Y, producing different eligibility sets.

source_clause: Do not proactively offer compensation unless the user explicitly asks for one.
ambiguous_version: Agents must not proactively offer all eligible passengers compensation for flight delays.
unambiguous_version: Agents must not proactively offer compensation for flight delays to any eligible passenger; compensation is offered only when a passenger explicitly requests it.
ambiguity_point: 'must not proactively offer all eligible passengers compensation' — 'not ... all' scope: (a) agents must not offer compensation to any passenger proactively; (b) agents need not offer compensation to every eligible passenger, but may offer it to some.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (not > all): No proactive compensation offers to any passenger — agents wait for explicit requests.
Interpretation B (all > not): Agents are not required to offer compensation to all passengers — selective proactive offers to some passengers are acceptable.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent might proactively inform some passengers about compensation eligibility while skipping others. Under Interpretation A the agent never proactively mentions compensation to anyone, which is the intended behavior.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate to a user.
annotation_rationale: Classic 'not … all' scope ambiguity: the negation can take wide scope (prohibiting all proactive offers) or narrow scope (prohibiting only complete coverage), yielding materially different compliance behaviors.

source_clause: The cabin must be consistent across all flights in the reservation when modifying.
ambiguous_version: Agents may upgrade passengers to business class or change connecting flight legs when modifying a reservation.
unambiguous_version: When modifying a reservation, agents may change connecting flight legs, but the cabin class must remain the same across all flights; upgrading to business class requires a separate process and cannot be combined with a leg change in the same modification.
ambiguity_point: 'may upgrade to business class or change connecting flight legs' — are these two independent permitted modifications, or does 'upgrade to business class' scope as a sub-type of 'change connecting flight legs'?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Two independent permitted modifications — agents may either upgrade cabin class OR change flight legs as separate operations.
Interpretation B: Only leg changes are permitted; 'upgrade to business' is listed as a type of change, meaning upgrades are only possible in the context of a leg change.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent processes a standalone business class upgrade. Under Interpretation B the agent refuses an upgrade-only request and requires a flight-leg change to accompany any cabin change.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, cabin: string, payment_method_id: string) — Updates flight legs and/or cabin in a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Coordination ambiguity: 'A or B' with disjuncts of different action types creates ambiguity about whether both are independently permitted or B is a subspecification of A.

source_clause: Only compensate if the user is a silver/gold member, has travel insurance, or flies business class.
ambiguous_version: Only compensate silver or gold members with travel insurance who fly business class.
unambiguous_version: Compensate a user if any one of the following is true: (a) the user is a silver or gold member, (b) the user has travel insurance, or (c) the user flies in the business cabin. Any single condition suffices; they are independent.
ambiguity_point: 'silver or gold members with travel insurance who fly business class' — are these three independent criteria joined by OR, or a single conjunctive profile requiring all three?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (conjunctive): All three attributes must be present — only a silver/gold member who also has insurance AND flies business is eligible.
Interpretation B (disjunctive): Any one attribute is sufficient — silver/gold membership, insurance, or business class each independently qualifies.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent denies compensation to a gold member in economy with no insurance. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly approves compensation based on gold membership alone.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate to the specified user.
annotation_rationale: Quantifier–coordination scope ambiguity: the phrase 'members with insurance who fly business' can be parsed as A AND B AND C (conjunctive) or as three independently sufficient conditions (disjunctive), with drastically different eligibility outcomes.

source_clause: Each extra checked bag beyond the free allowance costs $50.
ambiguous_version: Gold and silver members may check additional bags beyond the standard allowance at no charge.
unambiguous_version: Silver members receive one additional free checked bag beyond the standard allowance. Gold members receive two additional free checked bags beyond the standard allowance. Any bags beyond these extended allowances cost $50 each.
ambiguity_point: 'gold and silver members may check additional bags' — does 'additional' scope per-member-tier (each tier has its own distinct additional allowance) or collectively (gold and silver together share an undifferentiated additional allowance)?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (collective): Gold and silver members share the same undifferentiated 'additional bags at no charge' benefit without tier-specific quantities.
Interpretation B (distributive): Each tier (gold, silver) has its own specific additional allowance, with gold receiving more than silver.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent cannot determine how many free additional bags a silver vs. gold member gets and applies the same (possibly incorrect) allowance to both. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly applies tier-specific allowances.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_baggages(reservation_id: string, total_baggages: int, payment_method_id: string) — Updates the baggage count for a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Collective–distributive quantifier ambiguity: 'gold and silver members' as a collective subject creates ambiguity about whether the benefit applies uniformly to both (collective) or differentially per tier (distributive).

source_clause: If the user complains about a delayed flight and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a $50-per-passenger certificate.
ambiguous_version: Agents may offer compensation if a flight is delayed and the user requests a change or cancellation.
unambiguous_version: Agents may offer a $50-per-passenger certificate only if both conditions are met: (1) a flight in the reservation is delayed, AND (2) the user explicitly requests to change or cancel the reservation as a result. The agent must first process the change or cancellation, then offer the certificate.
ambiguity_point: 'if a flight is delayed and the user requests a change or cancellation' — does 'change or cancellation' scope as a single disjunctive request-type, or can the compensation be offered for either a delay report alone OR a change/cancel request alone?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (both conditions required): Compensation requires both a delayed flight AND a change/cancel request — neither alone qualifies.
Interpretation B (either condition sufficient): Compensation can be offered for a delay complaint alone, or for a change/cancel request alone, without requiring both.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent offers a certificate whenever a user requests any flight change, even without a delay. Under Interpretation A the agent correctly requires both the delay and the change/cancel request.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate.
annotation_rationale: Conditional–conjunction scope: 'if A and B' is read as requiring both conditions, but surface structure allows parsing where 'and' conjoins two independently sufficient triggers rather than jointly necessary conditions.

source_clause: A reservation can include at most 5 passengers.
ambiguous_version: Agents may book any number of passengers on connected flights up to the maximum allowed.
unambiguous_version: Agents may book up to 5 passengers total on a reservation, regardless of how many flight segments the reservation includes. The 5-passenger limit applies to the reservation as a whole, not per flight segment.
ambiguity_point: 'up to the maximum allowed' — does the maximum scope over the total reservation (one cap for all flights combined) or per flight segment (each leg has its own cap of up to 5)?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (per reservation): The 5-passenger cap applies to the entire reservation — at most 5 passengers across all segments.
Interpretation B (per segment): Each flight segment can have up to 5 passengers independently, allowing more than 5 unique passengers across a multi-leg itinerary.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent books a 3-leg trip with 4 passengers on each segment as different travelers, totaling 12 distinct passengers, without triggering the cap. Under Interpretation A 5 passengers total is the hard limit.
stripped_tool_desc: book_reservation(user_id: string, origin: string, destination: string, flight_type: string, cabin: string, flights: list, passengers: list, payment_methods: list, travel_insurance: bool, add_checked_baggages: int) — Books a new flight reservation.
annotation_rationale: Quantifier scope over domain of application: the maximum applies either to the reservation entity collectively or to each segment distributively, with different outcomes for multi-segment bookings.

source_clause: You should not make up any information or knowledge not provided by the user or the tools.
ambiguous_version: Agents must verify all order and product information before modifying or cancelling any pending order.
unambiguous_version: Before modifying or cancelling a pending order, agents must verify both the order information (status, items, payment) and any product information relevant to the modification by using the available lookup tools.
ambiguity_point: 'all order and product information' — does 'all' distribute over both 'order information' and 'product information' independently, or does it scope only over 'order information' with 'product information' as a separate (possibly optional) check?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (all distributes): Agents must verify all information of both types — comprehensive verification of both order and product details is required before any action.
Interpretation B (all scopes narrowly): 'All order information' must be verified; product information verification is a separate, optional step.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent might cancel an order without checking current product availability or pricing, missing relevant product-level constraints. Under Interpretation A both checks are required.
stripped_tool_desc: get_order_details(order_id: string) — Returns full details of an order. get_product_details(product_id: string) — Returns product details including available options.
annotation_rationale: Universal quantifier scope in NP-coordination: 'all [A and B]' is ambiguous between ∀(A) ∧ ∀(B) (all of each type) and ∀(A), B (all of A type, B mentioned separately). Different verification requirements result.

source_clause: The modify items action can only be called once and will change the order status to 'pending (items modified)'.
ambiguous_version: An agent may not modify items more than once in pending orders with multiple items.
unambiguous_version: An agent may modify the items of any pending order at most once, regardless of how many items the order contains. The one-time limit applies to the entire modify-items action, not per item.
ambiguity_point: 'more than once in pending orders with multiple items' — does the modification limit scope per-order (one modification per order) or per-item (one modification per individual item within an order)?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (per order): The entire order can only have its items modified once total — all item changes must be submitted in a single call.
Interpretation B (per item): Each individual item within an order can be modified at most once — multiple calls are allowed as long as each item is only touched once.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent allows a customer to call modify-items three times on a 3-item order (once per item). Under Interpretation A the agent correctly enforces a single modification call regardless of item count.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies items in a pending order. Action is irreversible after completion.
annotation_rationale: Quantifier scope over granularity level: 'more than once' can scope over the order entity or over each item entity within the order, producing different enforcement of the one-time limit.

source_clause: The total will be refunded via the original payment method immediately if it is a gift card, otherwise in 5 to 7 business days.
ambiguous_version: Exchanges and returns on delivered orders are refunded to the original payment method or a new gift card.
unambiguous_version: For returned delivered orders, refunds go to the original payment method or to an existing gift card (customer's choice). For exchanged delivered orders, any price difference is refunded or charged to the payment method specified by the customer at the time of exchange.
ambiguity_point: 'exchanges and returns … refunded to the original payment method or a new gift card' — does 'or a new gift card' apply to both exchanges and returns, or only to returns?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Both exchanges and returns can be refunded to either the original payment method or a new gift card.
Interpretation B: Only returns can be directed to a new gift card; exchanges use only the original payment method.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent offers a gift card as a refund option when processing an exchange. Under Interpretation B the agent only offers the original payment method for exchanges.
stripped_tool_desc: exchange_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Initiates an exchange for delivered order items.
annotation_rationale: Scope of disjunctive complement over conjoined subject: 'exchanges and returns [refunded to A or B]' is ambiguous about whether the B option (new gift card) applies to both subjects or only the nearer one (returns).

source_clause: You must deny any requests for tasks related to any other user.
ambiguous_version: Agents must not share order details or profile information about every user in the system.
unambiguous_version: Agents must not share the order details or profile information of any user other than the currently authenticated user; the current user's own information may be shared freely.
ambiguity_point: 'about every user' — does 'not … every' mean (a) agents must not share information about any user at all, or (b) agents need not share information about every user, implying selective sharing is permitted?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (not > every): Agents are prohibited from sharing information about any user — complete information blackout.
Interpretation B (every > not): Agents are not required to share information about every user — they may choose which users' info to share.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent even refuses to share the authenticated user's own order history. Under Interpretation B the agent shares current user info freely but might share other users' info selectively — a privacy violation.
stripped_tool_desc: get_user_details(user_id: string) — Returns profile information for a user. get_order_details(order_id: string) — Returns order details.
annotation_rationale: Negation–universal quantifier scope ambiguity in restriction context: NOT(∀x share(x)) vs. ∀x NOT(share(x) for other-users). Both readings are syntactically valid but produce opposite privacy enforcement behaviors.

source_clause: If any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and a transfer is needed.
ambiguous_version: Agents may not modify or cancel reservations where any flight segment or passenger has already departed.
unambiguous_version: Agents may not modify or cancel a reservation if any flight segment within that reservation has already been flown. Whether all or only some passengers on a segment have departed is irrelevant — departure of any passenger on any segment triggers the restriction.
ambiguity_point: 'any flight segment or passenger has already departed' — does the restriction trigger when any segment is flown OR when any individual passenger has departed, creating two independently sufficient triggers?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Two independent triggers — if any segment is departed OR if any individual passenger has departed, modification/cancellation is blocked.
Interpretation B: A compound trigger — the segment and passenger criteria are synonymous descriptions of the same condition (a segment departure).
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent refuses to process changes when even one passenger on a multi-passenger booking has checked in and departed while others have not. Under Interpretation B the restriction applies at the segment level only.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Updates flights in a reservation. cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Disjunctive trigger scope: 'segment or passenger' as the subject of a restriction clause creates ambiguity about whether these are two independent conditions (triggering separately) or two descriptions of the same condition.

source_clause: Payment for a booking may include at most one travel certificate, one credit card, and three gift cards.
ambiguous_version: Every passenger in a booking may pay using one certificate or one credit card.
unambiguous_version: A booking as a whole may include at most one travel certificate OR one credit card as part of its payment; this limit applies per booking, not per passenger.
ambiguity_point: 'every passenger … may pay using one certificate or one credit card' — does 'every passenger' distribute (each passenger has their own payment method allowance) or does it collectively describe the booking's payment structure?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (distributive): Each passenger may individually provide one certificate or one credit card — allowing up to 5 certificates in a 5-passenger booking.
Interpretation B (collective): The booking as a whole is limited to one certificate or one credit card total, shared across all passengers.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent accepts 3 certificates for a 3-passenger booking. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly limits the booking to one certificate or one credit card total.
stripped_tool_desc: book_reservation(user_id: string, origin: string, destination: string, flight_type: string, cabin: string, flights: list, passengers: list, payment_methods: list, travel_insurance: bool, add_checked_baggages: int) — Books a flight reservation.
annotation_rationale: Collective–distributive quantifier scope: 'every passenger' as subject creates ambiguity about whether payment limits apply per individual (distributive) or per booking entity (collective).

source_clause: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions.
ambiguous_version: Agents should not attempt to resolve all complaints before transferring to a human agent.
unambiguous_version: Agents are not required to attempt resolution of every complaint before transferring; they should transfer immediately when a request is clearly out of scope, without first attempting to handle it.
ambiguity_point: 'should not attempt to resolve all complaints before transferring' — wide-scope negation: agents should never attempt to resolve any complaint before transferring; narrow-scope: agents need not attempt to resolve every complaint before transferring (some can transfer directly).
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (not > all): Agents should not attempt to resolve any complaint prior to transfer — transfer immediately for all issues.
Interpretation B (all > not): Agents are not obligated to attempt resolution of every complaint — selective resolution before transfer is appropriate.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A agents transfer users for every complaint without attempting resolution, even for clearly in-scope requests. Under Interpretation B agents handle in-scope requests themselves and only transfer out-of-scope ones.
stripped_tool_desc: transfer_to_human_agents(summary: string) — Transfers the conversation to a human agent.
annotation_rationale: Negation–universal scope over procedure: NOT(∀x attempt(x) before transfer) vs. ∀x NOT(must-attempt(x)) before transfer. Wide-scope negation prohibits all pre-transfer attempts; narrow-scope merely removes a blanket requirement.

source_clause: Once the user has been authenticated, you can provide information about their order, product, and profile.
ambiguous_version: Agents may provide product information or order details to authenticated users and new callers.
unambiguous_version: Agents may provide product information to any caller including unauthenticated ones. Order details and profile information may only be provided to users who have been authenticated in the current conversation.
ambiguity_point: 'to authenticated users and new callers' — does the permission ('may provide product information or order details') scope over both recipient groups, or does each information type apply to a different recipient group?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Both product information and order details may be provided to both authenticated users and new unauthenticated callers.
Interpretation B: Product information may be provided to new callers, but order details require authentication — the two information types apply to different caller categories.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent shares a user's order history with an unauthenticated caller. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly restricts order details to authenticated users only.
stripped_tool_desc: get_order_details(order_id: string) — Returns order details. get_product_details(product_id: string) — Returns product information.
annotation_rationale: Permission scope over coordinated object and indirect-object: 'may provide [A or B] to [C and D]' is ambiguous about whether all combinations are permitted or the two information types map to distinct recipient categories.

source_clause: Confirm the facts before offering compensation.
ambiguous_version: Agents must confirm all flight details and passenger counts before processing any changes or offering compensation.
unambiguous_version: Before processing any flight change or cancellation, agents must confirm the relevant flight details. Before offering compensation, agents must separately confirm the specific facts that establish eligibility (delay or cancellation and passenger count). These are two distinct confirmation steps.
ambiguity_point: 'confirm all flight details and passenger counts before processing any changes or offering compensation' — does a single combined confirmation satisfy requirements for both operations, or does each operation require its own dedicated confirmation step?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: One combined confirmation of all details covers both flight changes and compensation offers.
Interpretation B: Two distinct confirmation steps are required — one for flight changes and a separate one specifically for compensation eligibility.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent confirms details once and then both modifies a flight and offers compensation in a single step. Under Interpretation B the agent must separately confirm compensation-specific facts before issuing a certificate.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate. update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Updates reservation flights.
annotation_rationale: Scope of pre-condition over disjunctive consequent: 'before [A or B]' allows one pre-condition to gate both consequents (single confirmation) or separate pre-conditions for each consequent (two confirmations).

source_clause: The origin and destination of the trip cannot be changed when modifying a flight.
ambiguous_version: Agents cannot change the origin or destination for any passenger or flight segment during modification.
unambiguous_version: During flight modification, the origin and destination of the overall trip (the first departure city and final arrival city) cannot be changed. Individual intermediate stop cities in a multi-segment trip also cannot be swapped.
ambiguity_point: 'cannot change the origin or destination for any passenger or flight segment' — does 'cannot change' scope over passengers and segments as separate dimensions of prohibition, or does 'any passenger or flight segment' form a single compound domain of application?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Two separate prohibitions — (1) cannot change origin/destination for any passenger, AND (2) cannot change origin/destination for any flight segment.
Interpretation B: A single prohibition applying to the trip entity: the trip's origin and destination (as defined at booking) cannot be changed, period.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent blocks any change that touches origin/destination at any level of granularity. Under Interpretation B the agent might allow renaming an intermediate stop if the overall trip origin and destination remain unchanged.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Updates the flight segments in a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Scope of modal negation over compound object: 'cannot change X for any [A or B]' is ambiguous between separate prohibitions per category and a unified prohibition over both categories as a single domain.

source_clause: There cannot be any change of product types, e.g. modify shirt to shoe.
ambiguous_version: Agents may modify each item in a pending order once or process an exchange for a delivered order of the same product type.
unambiguous_version: Agents may modify each item in a pending order exactly once (to a different option of the same product type). Separately, agents may process an exchange for a delivered order, but the exchanged item must be of the same product type as the original.
ambiguity_point: 'modify each item … once or process an exchange' — does 'of the same product type' scope over just 'exchange' or over both 'modify each item' and 'exchange'?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (narrow scope): 'Same product type' constrains only exchanges; item modifications have no same-type restriction.
Interpretation B (wide scope): 'Same product type' constrains both modifications and exchanges — both operations must stay within the same product type.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent modifies a pending order item from a shirt to shoes (cross-type), treating the same-type restriction as applying only to exchanges. Under Interpretation B both operations are restricted to same-type changes.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies items in a pending order. exchange_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Exchanges items in a delivered order.
annotation_rationale: Modifier scope over disjunctive VP: 'do A or B [of the same type]' is ambiguous about whether the post-hoc modifier constrains both disjuncts or only the final one (nearest-attachment reading).

source_clause: It is a business flight — one of the four conditions under which flight cancellation is permitted.
ambiguous_version: All business and basic economy passengers may cancel flights booked through the corporate portal.
unambiguous_version: Business cabin passengers may cancel their flights under the standard business-class cancellation rule, regardless of booking portal. Basic economy passengers may not cancel regardless of booking portal. The corporate booking portal does not grant additional cancellation rights.
ambiguity_point: 'all business and basic economy passengers' — does 'all' distribute separately (all business may cancel AND all basic economy may cancel) or does it describe a combined group differentiated from other passengers?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A (distributive): Both business passengers and basic economy passengers individually qualify for cancellation through the corporate portal.
Interpretation B (collective group): 'Business and basic economy' describes a collective passenger category distinct from standard economy, and only business within this group may cancel.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent cancels a basic economy ticket because the customer booked through the corporate portal. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly refuses — basic economy retains its no-cancellation rule.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels a flight reservation. Does not validate eligibility.
annotation_rationale: Universal quantifier distribution over conjoined NP: 'all [A and B]' is ambiguous between all(A) ∧ all(B) (each group qualifies independently) and all(A∪B) with further constraints (collective subject).

source_clause: The user must provide a payment method to pay or receive a refund of the price difference when modifying items.
ambiguous_version: Agents must collect a payment method when modifying items or processing returns for any pending order.
unambiguous_version: When modifying items in a pending order, agents must collect a payment method to cover any price difference between old and new items. When processing a return, agents must collect the customer's preferred refund destination (original payment method or a gift card). These are two distinct collection requirements.
ambiguity_point: 'collect a payment method when modifying items or processing returns' — does the same payment-method collection apply identically to both operations, or does each operation have its own payment-information requirement?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The same payment method collection step applies to both modifications and returns — one uniform procedure.
Interpretation B: Modifications require collecting a payment method for price differences; returns require collecting a refund destination — different information is needed for each.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent asks for a new payment method when processing a return even when the customer just wants a refund to the original method. Under Interpretation B the agent asks the correct question for each operation type.
stripped_tool_desc: return_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Initiates return and refund. modify_pending_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies pending order items.
annotation_rationale: Scope of requirement over disjunctive action: 'must collect X when [A or B]' is ambiguous between X being the same entity for both A and B, versus X referring to operation-specific variants for each disjunct.

source_clause: Do not compensate if the user is a regular member and has no travel insurance and flies (basic) economy.
ambiguous_version: Agents must not compensate regular members without travel insurance or basic economy passengers.
unambiguous_version: Agents must not compensate a user if ALL three conditions are true simultaneously: (1) the user is a regular member, AND (2) the user has no travel insurance, AND (3) the user flies in economy or basic economy cabin. If any one of these three conditions is absent, compensation may be appropriate.
ambiguity_point: 'regular members without travel insurance or basic economy passengers' — does the exclusion apply to (regular members without insurance) OR (basic economy passengers) as two independent groups, or to (regular members) who are (without insurance or in basic economy)?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Two separate excluded groups — regular members without insurance are excluded, AND basic economy passengers are excluded (regardless of membership).
Interpretation B: One conjunctive exclusion — users who are regular members AND (lack insurance OR fly basic economy) are excluded.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A a gold member flying basic economy is denied compensation because they fall in the 'basic economy passengers' excluded group. Under Interpretation B a gold member flying basic economy is still eligible because they are not a 'regular member'.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate.
annotation_rationale: Coordination ambiguity in NP modification: 'regular members without insurance or basic economy passengers' allows grouping as [regular members without insurance] OR [basic economy passengers] vs. [regular members] without [insurance or basic economy status].

source_clause: After user confirmation, the order status will be changed to 'cancelled' and the total will be refunded.
ambiguous_version: After confirming any pending cancellation or modification, agents must update the order status and notify the user.
unambiguous_version: After confirming a cancellation, agents must call the cancel tool to update the order status; the system will automatically refund the user — no separate notification is needed. After confirming a modification, agents must call the modify tool; they should then confirm the new order details to the user.
ambiguity_point: 'update the order status and notify the user' — does 'and' join two separate sequential steps that apply to both cancellations and modifications, or does each operation have its own post-confirmation procedure?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Both steps (update status + notify) apply uniformly to both cancellations and modifications.
Interpretation B: Post-confirmation procedures differ by operation type — cancellations only need status update while modifications need status update plus detail confirmation.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent sends an explicit notification message after both cancellations and modifications. Under Interpretation B the agent applies operation-specific post-confirmation behavior.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_pending_order(order_id: string, reason: string) — Cancels a pending order and triggers automatic refund.
annotation_rationale: Conjunction scope over coordinated subject: 'after confirming [A or B], do C and D' is ambiguous between C and D applying uniformly to both A and B, versus C and D being operation-specific where each operation has distinct requirements.

source_clause: The cabin cannot be changed if any flight in the reservation has already been flown.
ambiguous_version: Agents may not modify the cabin or change the flight legs if any passenger has checked in.
unambiguous_version: Agents may not modify the cabin class of a reservation if any flight segment has already been flown. Agents may not change flight legs once any passenger has completed check-in. These are two separate restrictions with different trigger conditions.
ambiguity_point: 'may not modify cabin or change flight legs if any passenger has checked in' — does 'if any passenger has checked in' scope as the trigger for both prohibitions (cabin change AND leg change) or only for leg changes?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Check-in is the trigger for both restrictions — any checked-in passenger blocks both cabin changes and leg changes.
Interpretation B: The check-in trigger applies only to leg changes; cabin changes are blocked by a different condition (any segment flown), not by check-in.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent refuses to change a cabin even when no flights have been flown but a passenger has checked in — potentially incorrect. Under Interpretation B the agent applies the appropriate trigger for each restriction type.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, cabin: string, payment_method_id: string) — Updates flights and/or cabin in a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Conditional scope over disjunctive restriction: 'may not [do A or B] if C' is ambiguous between the conditional C scoping over both A and B versus applying only to the nearer disjunct B.

source_clause: The user needs to confirm the reason for cancellation (either 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake').
ambiguous_version: The agent must obtain a valid reason from the user before cancelling a pending order.
unambiguous_version: The agent must obtain a reason from the user before cancelling a pending order, and the reason must be exactly one of: 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake'. Any other stated reason is not acceptable.
ambiguity_point: 'valid reason' — valid may mean (a) one of the two enumerated acceptable reasons; (b) any reason that is logically coherent or plausible; (c) any reason the customer sincerely holds.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Valid' means from the closed list of two accepted reasons — the agent must reject any reason outside 'no longer needed' / 'ordered by mistake'.
Interpretation B: 'Valid' means any genuine, non-frivolous customer reason — the agent accepts reasons like 'found a better price' or 'changed my mind'.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent accepts 'I found a cheaper option elsewhere' and proceeds with cancellation. Under Interpretation A the agent correctly rejects this reason and asks the customer to provide one of the two permitted reasons.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_pending_order(order_id: string, reason: string) — Cancels a pending order with the specified reason.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'valid': in everyday English 'valid reason' means any defensible reason; in a constrained policy context it means a reason from a closed enumerated set. The intended policy sense is not determinable without the enumeration.

source_clause: An order can only be cancelled if its status is 'pending'.
ambiguous_version: The agent can cancel orders that have not yet been processed.
unambiguous_version: The agent can cancel orders whose status is exactly 'pending'. Orders with status 'processed', 'delivered', or 'cancelled' cannot be cancelled.
ambiguity_point: 'not yet been processed' — processed may mean (a) the specific order status 'processed' in the system; (b) handled in any way by the warehouse or shipping system; (c) charged to the payment method.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Not yet processed' means status is not 'processed' — covers both 'pending' and potentially orders in other non-final states.
Interpretation B: 'Not yet processed' means status is specifically 'pending' — the only cancellable state.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent might attempt to cancel a 'delivered' order on grounds that it is 'not processed' in the warehouse sense. Under Interpretation B only 'pending' status orders are cancellable.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_pending_order(order_id: string, reason: string) — Cancels an order. Returns error if order is not in a cancellable state.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'processed': the word has a domain-specific meaning (a specific order status value) and a common English meaning (handled/acted upon). Without seeing the status enum, an agent may adopt the colloquial meaning.

source_clause: The modify items action will change the order status to 'pending (items modified)' and the agent will not be able to modify or cancel the order anymore.
ambiguous_version: Once items have been modified, the order is locked and no further changes are permitted.
unambiguous_version: Once the modify_pending_order_items tool has been called, the order status changes to 'pending (items modified)' and the agent cannot call modify_pending_order_items or cancel_pending_order on that order again. The payment method may still be updated.
ambiguity_point: 'locked' and 'no further changes' — 'changes' may mean (a) only item modifications; (b) all modifications including payment; (c) any action including returns after delivery.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'No further changes' means no modifications of any kind, including payment method changes — the order is fully frozen.
Interpretation B: 'No further changes' refers only to item-level modifications; payment method can still be updated.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent refuses a customer's request to update the payment method after items have been modified. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly processes the payment update.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_payment(order_id: string, payment_method_id: string) — Updates the payment method of a pending order.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'changes' and 'locked': these terms lack defined scope — whether they apply to all operations or only item modifications is not determinable from context alone.

source_clause: If the user provides a gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the price difference.
ambiguous_version: The customer must provide adequate payment when modifying order items with a price difference.
unambiguous_version: When modifying order items with a price increase, the customer must provide a payment method with sufficient balance or credit to cover the price difference. If a gift card is provided, its current balance must be greater than or equal to the price difference.
ambiguity_point: 'adequate payment' — adequate may mean (a) any payment method that technically works (credit card with no balance check); (b) payment with verified sufficient balance; (c) payment pre-approved for the exact difference amount.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Adequate payment' means any payment method presented — the agent accepts a gift card without checking balance.
Interpretation B: 'Adequate payment' requires verified sufficient balance — the agent must check gift card balance before proceeding.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent accepts a gift card with $5 balance to cover a $50 price difference and calls the tool, which then fails. Under Interpretation B the agent proactively checks the gift card balance and declines if insufficient.
stripped_tool_desc: get_user_details(user_id: string) — Returns user profile including payment methods and gift card balances.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'adequate': the term is graded and lacks a defined threshold. In financial contexts it could mean technically valid, sufficiently funded, or pre-authorized — three distinct verification procedures.

source_clause: Return delivered order: the refund will be to the original payment method or a gift card.
ambiguous_version: Refunds for returned items will be credited back to the customer's account.
unambiguous_version: Refunds for returned items will be applied to the original payment method used for the purchase (PayPal, credit card, or gift card) or to an existing gift card in the customer's account, as chosen by the customer.
ambiguity_point: 'credited back to the customer's account' — 'account' may mean (a) the specific payment method used for the original purchase; (b) a general store account or wallet; (c) any payment method on file; (d) a store credit balance.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Refund goes to the customer's store account or store credit balance — not necessarily the original payment method.
Interpretation B: Refund goes to the original payment method — the word 'account' refers specifically to that method.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent issues store credit and considers the return resolved. Under Interpretation B the agent refunds to the original PayPal/credit card/gift card as the customer paid.
stripped_tool_desc: return_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Initiates a return. The payment_method_id specifies the refund destination.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'account': in retail contexts 'account' can refer to the user's platform account (with a store credit balance), the specific payment method used, or any on-file payment method. Each leads to different refund routing.

source_clause: You should deny user requests that are against this policy.
ambiguous_version: Agents should decline requests that fall outside the scope of permitted retail operations.
unambiguous_version: Agents must refuse to execute any request that is explicitly prohibited by or not covered in this policy. For requests that are not covered (i.e., out of scope), agents should transfer the user to a human agent rather than attempting to handle them.
ambiguity_point: 'decline' — may mean (a) refuse and provide no further assistance; (b) refuse but offer alternatives; (c) mark as declined in the system; (d) deprioritize but eventually handle.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Decline' means actively refuse with an explanation and stop — no further action on the request.
Interpretation B: 'Decline' means not execute directly but still assist indirectly (e.g., transfer to human, provide information about alternative channels).
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent simply says 'I cannot help with that' and ends the interaction. Under Interpretation B the agent refuses the specific action but transfers to a human or explains the alternative path.
stripped_tool_desc: transfer_to_human_agents(summary: string) — Transfers the conversation to a human agent.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'decline': in customer service contexts, 'decline' can mean refuse-and-close, refuse-and-redirect, or deprioritize. The procedural consequence (transfer vs. terminate) depends heavily on which sense is adopted.

source_clause: For a pending order, each item can be modified to an available new item of the same product but of different product option.
ambiguous_version: Items in a pending order can be swapped for any available alternative of the same kind.
unambiguous_version: Items in a pending order can be replaced with a different variant (option) of the same product type. For example, a size M blue shirt can be changed to a size L blue shirt or a size M red shirt — but not to a different product type like pants.
ambiguity_point: 'same kind' — 'kind' may mean (a) same product type (e.g., shirt vs. shirt); (b) same product with different variant options; (c) same general category (e.g., clothing); (d) same price range.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Same kind' means same general product category (e.g., any clothing item) — a shirt can be swapped for pants.
Interpretation B: 'Same kind' means same specific product type — shirt for shirt only, with different option (color, size).
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent modifies a shirt to pants because both are 'clothing'. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly refuses the cross-type swap.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies items in a pending order.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'kind': the term has multiple granularity levels (category, type, variant). Without defining the level, an agent may apply a broader or narrower interpretation than the policy intends.

source_clause: At the beginning of the conversation, you have to authenticate the user identity by locating their user id via email, or via name + zip code.
ambiguous_version: Before assisting a customer, the agent must verify the customer's identity.
unambiguous_version: Before assisting a customer, the agent must locate the customer's user ID either by asking for their email address or by asking for their full name and zip code. This step is required even if the customer provides their user ID directly.
ambiguity_point: 'verify identity' — may mean (a) locate user ID via email or name+zip (the policy-specified method); (b) ask for any identifying information the customer provides; (c) confirm the user's stated identity without system lookup; (d) request a password or PIN.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Identity verification means the agent must look up the user ID via one of two specified methods (email or name+zip), regardless of what the customer provides.
Interpretation B: Identity verification means accepting whatever identifying information the customer provides (including self-stated user IDs, order numbers, etc.).
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent accepts a customer-stated user ID without performing the email or name+zip lookup, bypassing the authentication requirement. Under Interpretation A the lookup is always required.
stripped_tool_desc: find_user_id_by_email(email: string) — Finds user ID by email. find_user_id_by_name_zip(first_name: string, last_name: string, zip: string) — Finds user ID by name and zip.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'verify': in security contexts, 'verify' can mean confirm-against-system (requiring a lookup) or accept-as-stated (trusting the customer's claim). The policy-intended sense requires the system lookup, but the common English sense of 'verify' could allow acceptance of a provided ID.

source_clause: You can only help one user per conversation but can handle multiple requests from the same user.
ambiguous_version: The agent must handle each customer's requests individually within a single session.
unambiguous_version: The agent may handle multiple requests from the same authenticated user within a single conversation, but must not assist any other user during that conversation. If a different user needs assistance, they must start a new conversation.
ambiguity_point: 'individually' — may mean (a) one request at a time, sequentially within the same session; (b) each customer gets their own separate session; (c) each request must be handled without combining with others.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Individually' means one request per session — only a single request per conversation is permitted, even for the same user.
Interpretation B: 'Individually' means each request is addressed in turn — multiple requests from the same user are handled sequentially in one session.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent ends the conversation after completing one request and requires a new session for the user's second request. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly handles the user's second request in the same session.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'individually': the adverb can mean 'one at a time in sequence' (allowing multiple sequential requests) or 'each in a separate instance' (requiring separate sessions per request). The policy intent is the former.

source_clause: The modify items action can only be called once and the agent will not be able to modify or cancel the order anymore.
ambiguous_version: Modifications to an order's items are final and the order record becomes read-only.
unambiguous_version: After the modify_pending_order_items tool is called, no further calls to modify or cancel that specific order are allowed. The order status changes to 'pending (items modified)'. The agent can still look up order details but cannot execute further changes.
ambiguity_point: 'read-only' and 'final' — may mean (a) no tool calls that change the order are permitted; (b) the agent cannot display or discuss the order; (c) the order record is archived and inaccessible.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Read-only' means the agent can view but not change — lookups are still permitted, only modifications are blocked.
Interpretation B: 'Read-only' means no further interaction with the order record — the agent refuses to even display order details.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent refuses to look up and confirm order details after modification, leaving the customer without confirmation of what was changed. Under Interpretation A the agent correctly displays the updated order details.
stripped_tool_desc: get_order_details(order_id: string) — Returns current order details including status, items, and payment.
annotation_rationale: Technical term polysemy: 'read-only' in database contexts means no writes are permitted but reads are still allowed. However in everyday English 'final' can imply the record is closed entirely. The operational consequence differs significantly.

source_clause: Flight can be cancelled if the booking was made within the last 24 hours.
ambiguous_version: Passengers may cancel flights booked recently without penalty.
unambiguous_version: Passengers may cancel a flight booking made within the last 24 hours without penalty. 'Within the last 24 hours' is calculated from the current time to the time the booking was created, not from the scheduled departure time.
ambiguity_point: 'recently' — may mean (a) within 24 hours of booking creation; (b) within 24 hours of departure; (c) within the same calendar day; (d) within a few days.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Recently' means within 24 hours of the booking creation timestamp.
Interpretation B: 'Recently' means within some other time window — same day, 48 hours, or within 24 hours of departure.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent cancels a booking made 30 hours ago because 'it seems recent enough.' Under Interpretation A the agent correctly enforces the 24-hour window from booking creation.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels a reservation. Does not enforce eligibility.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'recently': the adverb lacks a defined threshold and can be interpreted as various time windows. In airline policy '24 hours from booking' is the specific rule, but 'recently' could imply same-day or other windows.

source_clause: It is a business flight — one of the four cancellation eligibility conditions.
ambiguous_version: Corporate travel bookings are eligible for cancellation under the business travel exception.
unambiguous_version: A booking is eligible for cancellation under the business travel exception if and only if the cabin class of all flights in the reservation is 'business'. Corporate account bookings in economy or basic economy are not eligible under this exception.
ambiguity_point: 'Corporate travel bookings' and 'business travel' — 'business' may mean (a) business cabin class; (b) bookings made for corporate/work purposes; (c) bookings made through a corporate account.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Business travel' means the cabin class is business — the flight is in the business cabin.
Interpretation B: 'Business travel' means the purpose of the trip is work-related — any cabin class qualifies if the passenger is traveling for business.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent cancels an economy booking because the passenger claims it was for a work conference. Under Interpretation A the agent only applies the exception to actual business-cabin bookings.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels a reservation. Agent must verify eligibility before calling.
annotation_rationale: Domain-specific polysemy of 'business': in airline policy 'business' refers to the business cabin class; in everyday English it refers to commercial/work purpose. Both readings are plausible without the domain definition.

source_clause: The user has travel insurance and the reason for cancellation is covered by insurance.
ambiguous_version: The agent may cancel a flight if the customer's cancellation reason is covered.
unambiguous_version: The agent may cancel a flight if the customer has travel insurance and the stated reason for cancellation is listed as a covered reason in their insurance policy. The agent must ask the customer to confirm that their insurance covers the stated reason.
ambiguity_point: 'covered' — may mean (a) covered by travel insurance specifically; (b) covered by any policy including corporate reimbursement; (c) covered under general airline cancellation rules; (d) reasonable/understandable.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Covered' means specifically covered under the customer's travel insurance policy.
Interpretation B: 'Covered' means any form of coverage or justification — corporate policies, compelling personal reasons, or general airline rules.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent cancels a flight for a customer who says their employer 'covers' the trip cost, treating employer reimbursement as equivalent to insurance coverage. Under Interpretation A the agent requires actual travel insurance coverage.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'covered' in insurance context: the word can mean covered by the specific travel insurance product, or more broadly covered/justified in any sense. The policy intends the narrow insurance-specific meaning.

source_clause: Do not proactively offer compensation unless the user explicitly asks for one.
ambiguous_version: Agents should not bring up compensation unless the customer raises the issue.
unambiguous_version: Agents must not mention, suggest, or hint at compensation eligibility unless the customer explicitly uses words like 'compensation', 'certificate', 'refund for the delay/cancellation', or directly asks what they are entitled to. Oblique references such as 'I'm very unhappy' do not count as raising the issue.
ambiguity_point: 'raises the issue' and 'explicitly asks' — 'raises' may mean (a) directly asks using the word 'compensation'; (b) complains about the inconvenience in any form; (c) implies interest without directly requesting.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Raises the issue' means any expression of dissatisfaction — a complaint about a delay counts, triggering compensation discussion.
Interpretation B: 'Raises the issue' means a direct, explicit request for compensation — general complaints do not trigger the offer.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent proactively offers compensation whenever a customer says 'this delay is really frustrating.' Under Interpretation B the agent only offers when the customer directly asks about compensation.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'raises/explicitly asks': 'raises the issue' spans a spectrum from any complaint (broad) to direct request (narrow). The policy intends the narrow sense but the term admits the broader reading.

source_clause: Confirm the facts before offering compensation.
ambiguous_version: The agent must establish the situation before issuing any certificate.
unambiguous_version: Before issuing a compensation certificate, the agent must confirm with the customer: (1) the specific flight(s) affected, (2) whether those flights were cancelled or delayed, and (3) the number of passengers on the affected flights.
ambiguity_point: 'establish the situation' — may mean (a) verify specific factual claims (flight cancelled, delay duration, passenger count); (b) understand the customer's emotional state; (c) document the complaint for records; (d) confirm eligibility criteria are met.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Establish' means gathering enough customer context to understand their complaint — no specific fact-checking required.
Interpretation B: 'Establish' means verifying specific factual claims (cancellation/delay, passenger count) before issuing the certificate.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent issues a certificate after listening to the customer's complaint without verifying whether the flight was actually delayed or how many passengers were affected. Under Interpretation B the agent verifies both before calculating and issuing the certificate.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate to a user.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'establish': the verb can mean assess contextually (understanding) or verify factually (checking against records). The policy intends specific fact-checking but the term allows a looser interpretation.

source_clause: Basic economy is a cabin class completely distinct from economy.
ambiguous_version: Economy-class rules apply to all non-premium cabin passengers.
unambiguous_version: Standard economy rules apply only to passengers booked in the 'economy' cabin. Basic economy is a separate cabin class with its own more restrictive rules — basic economy passengers cannot modify their reservations regardless of circumstances.
ambiguity_point: 'non-premium cabin' — may mean (a) economy only; (b) both economy and basic economy; (c) all cabins other than business.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Non-premium' covers both economy and basic economy — basic economy passengers receive economy rules.
Interpretation B: 'Non-premium' refers only to standard economy; basic economy is treated as a distinct cabin with stricter rules.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent allows a basic economy passenger to modify their flight because economy-class rules permit modification. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly refuses modification for basic economy.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Updates flights in a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Vague category boundary: 'non-premium' is not a defined term in airline policy. Whether it includes only economy or also basic economy is ambiguous — and the distinction has critical operational consequences.

source_clause: The API does not check that cancellation rules are met, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API.
ambiguous_version: Agents are responsible for ensuring compliance before executing flight cancellations.
unambiguous_version: Agents must manually verify that at least one of the four cancellation eligibility conditions is satisfied before calling the cancel_reservation tool. The cancel_reservation tool will execute the cancellation regardless of eligibility — the agent is the only safeguard.
ambiguity_point: 'ensuring compliance' — may mean (a) verifying the four specific eligibility conditions before calling the tool; (b) following the conversation protocol (confirmation, documentation); (c) checking that the tool call format is correct.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Compliance' refers to process compliance (following conversation steps) — not necessarily checking the four substantive eligibility conditions.
Interpretation B: 'Compliance' means verifying the four cancellation eligibility conditions — substantive policy compliance before the tool call.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent calls the cancellation tool after getting user confirmation but without checking whether any of the four eligibility conditions apply. Under Interpretation B the agent explicitly verifies eligibility before proceeding.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels the specified reservation immediately. No eligibility check is performed.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'compliance': in procedural contexts 'compliance' can refer to process/format compliance or substantive rule compliance. The policy requires substantive eligibility checking, but the term alone does not convey this.

source_clause: The flight is cancelled by the airline — one of the four conditions under which a passenger's booking can be cancelled.
ambiguous_version: Agents may cancel a reservation when the airline has cancelled the service.
unambiguous_version: Agents may cancel a reservation when the airline has cancelled one or more of the specific flights in that reservation. A general service suspension (e.g., the airline pausing a route temporarily) that has not yet cancelled the customer's specific scheduled flight does not qualify.
