ambiguity_point: 'cancelled the service' — 'service' may mean (a) the specific flight(s) in the customer's reservation; (b) the route in general; (c) the airline's operations on that day.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Service' means the specific flights booked — only the customer's actual flights being cancelled triggers eligibility.
Interpretation B: 'Service' means the route or general service — any operational disruption on the route qualifies.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent cancels a booking because the airline announced route suspensions next month, even though the customer's specific flight is still scheduled. Under Interpretation A only an actual cancellation of the customer's flight qualifies.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels the reservation.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'service': airlines use 'service' to mean a specific flight, a route, or general operations. The policy intends the narrow sense (specific flight), but 'service' commonly refers to broader operational categories.

source_clause: If the user complains about a cancelled flight, the agent can offer a $100-per-passenger certificate as a gesture.
ambiguous_version: When a customer reports a flight disruption, the agent may offer an appropriate gesture of goodwill.
unambiguous_version: When a customer reports that a flight in their reservation was cancelled by the airline, and the customer explicitly asks for compensation, the agent may offer a certificate of $100 per passenger in the reservation as a gesture of goodwill.
ambiguity_point: 'appropriate gesture of goodwill' — may mean (a) the specific $100-per-passenger certificate; (b) any form of goodwill (apology, miles, priority boarding); (c) a variable amount at agent discretion.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Appropriate gesture' means the specifically mandated $100-per-passenger certificate — no other form is permitted.
Interpretation B: 'Appropriate gesture' allows the agent to choose any form of compensation (miles, service upgrades, variable dollar amounts) based on the situation.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent offers 500 frequent flyer miles or a $50 voucher at their discretion. Under Interpretation A the agent correctly offers only the $100-per-passenger certificate as specified.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate of the specified amount.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'appropriate gesture of goodwill': the phrase abstracts away the specific policy requirement ($100 per passenger, certificates only). Different agents will apply different standards for 'appropriate'.

source_clause: The cabin must be consistent across all flights in the reservation when modifying.
ambiguous_version: All flights in a modified reservation must have matching travel class.
unambiguous_version: After modification, all flights within a reservation must be in the same cabin class (e.g., all economy or all business). Mixing cabin classes across segments (e.g., one economy leg and one business leg) is not permitted.
ambiguity_point: 'matching travel class' — 'matching' and 'travel class' may mean (a) all segments in the same named cabin (economy, business, basic economy); (b) same general tier (premium vs. non-premium); (c) same fare class code.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Matching' means all flights in the exact same named cabin — economy with economy, business with business.
Interpretation B: 'Matching' means all flights in a broadly comparable tier — economy and basic economy could both count as 'matching' because they are both non-premium.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent modifies a reservation to mix economy and basic economy segments, treating them as 'matching' non-premium travel classes. Under Interpretation A the agent correctly refuses because basic economy and economy are distinct cabins.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, cabin: string, payment_method_id: string) — Updates reservation flights.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'matching travel class': 'matching' could mean exact cabin name matching or tier-level matching. Given that basic economy is a distinct cabin, the intended meaning is exact-name matching, but the term allows tier-based grouping.

source_clause: Exchange delivered order: same product type constraint applies.
ambiguous_version: Customers may exchange delivered items for equivalent products.
unambiguous_version: Customers may exchange delivered items for a different variant (option) of the same product type. The exchanged item must be of the same product type (e.g., shirt for shirt) but can be a different size, color, or other option.
ambiguity_point: 'equivalent products' — 'equivalent' may mean (a) same product type with different options; (b) same price point; (c) similar functionality or category; (d) same product ID.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Equivalent' means same price range — a $30 item can be exchanged for any other $30 item regardless of type.
Interpretation B: 'Equivalent' means same product type — only exchanges within the same product category are permitted.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent processes an exchange of a shirt for a pair of headphones because both are priced at $30. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly refuses and requires the exchange to stay within the same product type.
stripped_tool_desc: exchange_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Processes an exchange for delivered items.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'equivalent': the word can mean price-equivalent, function-equivalent, or type-equivalent. Policy intends type-equivalent (same product type), but the term without definition admits price or functional equivalence.

source_clause: Modify payment: the new payment method must not be the same as the existing one.
ambiguous_version: The replacement payment method must be different from the one currently on the order.
unambiguous_version: The replacement payment method must have a different payment method ID than the one currently associated with the order. Two gift cards are considered different payment methods if they have different IDs, even if they belong to the same user.
ambiguity_point: 'different from' — may mean (a) a different payment method ID (technically different record); (b) a different payment method type (e.g., can't replace credit card with another credit card); (c) functionally different in some way.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Different' means a different payment method type — cannot replace a Visa credit card with another credit card, even from a different bank.
Interpretation B: 'Different' means a different specific payment method ID — any payment method record that is not the exact same stored method qualifies.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent refuses to replace one credit card with a different credit card because they are 'the same type.' Under Interpretation B the agent correctly accepts the change as long as the new card has a different ID.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_payment(order_id: string, payment_method_id: string) — Updates the payment method of a pending order.
annotation_rationale: Ambiguity in 'different': the comparison can be at the record level (different ID) or at the type level (different payment instrument class). The policy intends record-level difference, but 'different payment method' could imply type-level difference.

source_clause: You should at most make one tool call at a time and if you make a tool call you should not respond to the user at the same time.
ambiguous_version: The agent must complete one transaction at a time before initiating another.
unambiguous_version: In each turn of the conversation, the agent must choose between either sending a message to the user or making one tool call. Both actions cannot occur in the same turn. The agent may make multiple tool calls across successive turns to complete a complex request.
ambiguity_point: 'complete one transaction at a time' — 'transaction' may mean (a) a single tool call per turn; (b) a complete end-to-end customer request (all related tool calls together); (c) a single database operation.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Transaction' means a complete customer request — the agent must finish all steps of the current request before starting another (no interleaving).
Interpretation B: 'Transaction' means a single tool call — the agent may initiate different requests alternately across turns, one tool call per turn.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent refuses to partially address a cancellation and then start discussing a return until the cancellation is fully resolved. Under Interpretation B the agent can freely interleave tool calls for different requests across turns.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'transaction': in database terminology a transaction is an atomic unit of work; in customer service it can mean a complete service episode. These map to different sequential constraints on agent behavior.

source_clause: You should not make up any information or knowledge not provided by the user or the tools.
ambiguous_version: Agents should only communicate information they can directly support.
unambiguous_version: Agents should only communicate information that was explicitly provided by the customer during the conversation or returned by a tool call. Agents must not infer, estimate, or state facts not grounded in these two sources.
ambiguity_point: 'can directly support' — may mean (a) information explicitly provided by user or tool; (b) information inferable from context or common knowledge; (c) information the agent is reasonably confident about.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Directly support' means provably grounded in user input or tool output — no inference or estimation.
Interpretation B: 'Directly support' means the agent believes it to be correct based on reasoning — informed inference is acceptable.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent says 'Your order will probably arrive tomorrow based on the shipping date' without querying the tracking tool. Under Interpretation A the agent only states delivery information after confirming it via a tool call.
stripped_tool_desc: get_order_details(order_id: string) — Returns current order details.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'directly support': in epistemological contexts 'supporting' evidence can mean proof (strict) or plausibility (loose). The policy intends the strict reading (explicitly provided data only), but the phrasing admits informed inference.

source_clause: If the user complains about a delayed flight and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a $50-per-passenger certificate.
ambiguous_version: Agents may issue a delay certificate when the customer's flight was significantly delayed.
unambiguous_version: Agents may issue a $50-per-passenger certificate when a flight in the customer's reservation was delayed — for any duration of delay — provided the customer explicitly requests a change or cancellation of the reservation as a result.
ambiguity_point: 'significantly delayed' — 'significant' is not defined; may mean (a) any delay; (b) delay exceeding a specific threshold (e.g., 2 hours, 3 hours); (c) a delay causing a missed connection; (d) a delay the customer considers significant.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Significant' requires a minimum delay duration (e.g., 2+ hours) before compensation is warranted.
Interpretation B: Any delay — even 15 minutes — qualifies if the customer complains about it.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent asks the customer how long the delay was before offering compensation, potentially denying a $50 certificate for a 45-minute delay. Under Interpretation B the agent offers compensation for any reported delay the customer complains about.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'significant': the term is graded and subjective. Different agents will apply different thresholds, producing inconsistent compensation decisions. The actual policy specifies no minimum delay duration.

source_clause: A reservation can include at most one travel certificate as part of the payment.
ambiguous_version: Only one promotional instrument may be applied per booking.
unambiguous_version: Only one travel certificate may be applied per booking. Gift cards and credit cards are not considered promotional instruments and are not subject to this limit.
ambiguity_point: 'promotional instrument' — may mean (a) only travel certificates; (b) travel certificates and gift cards; (c) any discount or non-standard payment form (certificates, gift cards, miles).
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Promotional instrument' covers certificates, gift cards, and potentially miles — only one of any such type can be applied.
Interpretation B: 'Promotional instrument' means only certificates — gift cards are regular payment methods not subject to this limit.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent refuses to accept two gift cards because they treat gift cards as 'promotional instruments.' Under Interpretation B the agent correctly allows up to three gift cards alongside a certificate.
stripped_tool_desc: book_reservation(user_id: string, origin: string, destination: string, flight_type: string, cabin: string, flights: list, passengers: list, payment_methods: list, travel_insurance: bool, add_checked_baggages: int) — Books a reservation with specified payment methods.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'promotional instrument': in payment processing, promotional instruments typically include certificates and gift cards; in marketing, the term covers any discount mechanism. The distinction determines which payment limits apply.

source_clause: The trip type (one-way or round-trip) cannot be changed when modifying a reservation.
ambiguous_version: Agents cannot change the structure of a reservation during modification.
unambiguous_version: During modification, agents cannot change the trip type (one-way vs. round-trip), the origin airport, or the destination airport. Flight-segment details (dates, times, flight numbers) within the existing structure may be changed.
ambiguity_point: 'structure of a reservation' — 'structure' may mean (a) trip type and origin/destination only; (b) any fixed booking parameter including number of passengers or cabin; (c) the entire booking configuration.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Structure' is narrow — only trip type and origin/destination are fixed; everything else can be modified.
Interpretation B: 'Structure' is broad — any major booking parameter (passengers, cabin, trip type, routing) counts as structural and cannot be changed.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent refuses to change a cabin class or passenger count because these are 'structural.' Under Interpretation A the agent only blocks changes to trip type and origin/destination, allowing cabin and passenger modifications per other rules.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Updates flight segments in a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Vagueness of 'structure': in software engineering, structure refers to the template/schema; in travel, it could mean routing, booking class, or trip type. Without definition, agents may apply overly broad or narrow restrictions.

source_clause: Return delivered order: items must have been delivered (status is 'delivered').
ambiguous_version: The return process applies to orders the customer has received.
unambiguous_version: The return process applies only to orders whose status in the system is 'delivered'. Orders in transit, pending, or processed status are not eligible for return processing.
ambiguity_point: 'received' — may mean (a) the system status is 'delivered'; (b) the customer physically has the item in hand; (c) the carrier has delivered to the address (which may differ from customer receipt).
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Received' means the system status is 'delivered' — the database state triggers eligibility.
Interpretation B: 'Received' means the customer physically confirms receipt — a customer could claim receipt before the status updates, or dispute receipt when the status says delivered.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent processes a return for an order the customer claims to have received, even though the system shows status 'processed'. Under Interpretation A the agent checks the database status and only proceeds when status is 'delivered'.
stripped_tool_desc: return_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Initiates a return. Returns error if order is not in delivered status.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'received': the word can refer to the system-recorded delivery event (database status) or the customer's physical receipt (self-reported). These two can diverge and lead to different eligibility decisions.

source_clause: Gold members receive 4 free checked bags in business class.
ambiguous_version: Premium-tier travelers in upper-cabin seats receive the maximum checked baggage allowance.
unambiguous_version: Gold-tier members booked in the business cabin receive 4 free checked bags. This is the maximum allowance in the system. Silver, regular, and all economy/basic-economy travelers receive fewer free bags according to the baggage table.
ambiguity_point: 'premium-tier' and 'upper-cabin' — 'premium-tier' may mean gold only or gold+silver; 'upper-cabin' may mean business only or business+economy (vs. basic economy).
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Premium-tier' = gold only; 'upper-cabin' = business only — only gold members in business get maximum allowance.
Interpretation B: 'Premium-tier' = silver and gold; 'upper-cabin' = economy and business — silver members in economy also receive maximum allowance.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent allows a silver member booking economy to add 4 free bags. Under Interpretation A only gold-business travelers receive 4 free bags; silver members in economy get fewer.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_baggages(reservation_id: string, total_baggages: int, payment_method_id: string) — Updates checked baggage count.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of category labels: 'premium-tier' and 'upper-cabin' are informal synonyms for membership and cabin tiers respectively, but their exact coverage (which tiers qualify) is ambiguous without explicit mapping to the defined tier names.

source_clause: You can only help one user per conversation and must deny any requests for tasks related to any other user.
ambiguous_version: The agent must decline requests made on behalf of another party.
unambiguous_version: The agent must refuse to perform any action (lookups, cancellations, modifications, returns) related to a user account other than the one that was authenticated at the start of the current conversation.
ambiguity_point: 'on behalf of another party' — 'another party' may mean (a) a different user account; (b) any third party including the customer's family member at the same address; (c) a business entity; (d) anyone other than the authenticated account holder.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Another party' means any user other than the authenticated account — even a spouse making a request about their own account is refused.
Interpretation B: 'Another party' means an unauthorized third party — if the customer has authority over the other account (e.g., family manager), requests can be handled.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation B an agent helps a user manage their spouse's order because the customer claims shared account authority. Under Interpretation A the agent correctly refuses to take any action on any account other than the authenticated one.
stripped_tool_desc: get_user_details(user_id: string) — Returns user profile. get_order_details(order_id: string) — Returns order details.
annotation_rationale: Polysemy of 'another party': in legal contexts a 'party' is any distinct legal entity; in customer service it may connote unauthorized third parties vs. authorized representatives. The intended meaning is any other user account, but the term allows relationship-based exceptions.

source_clause: An order can only be cancelled if its status is 'pending', and the user must confirm the reason.
ambiguous_version: A pending order may be cancelled upon user request with a stated reason.
unambiguous_version: A pending order may be cancelled upon user request. The user must state a reason, and the reason must be either 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake'. Requests with any other stated reason must be declined.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify what reasons are acceptable — it only says a reason must be stated.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Any stated reason is sufficient — the agent accepts 'I found it cheaper elsewhere' or 'I changed my mind'.
Interpretation B: Only the two enumerated reasons are acceptable — the agent must reject all others.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent cancels an order for a customer who says 'I just don't want it anymore' (which is not one of the two valid reasons). Under Interpretation B the agent asks the customer to rephrase as one of the two permitted reasons.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_pending_order(order_id: string, reason: string) — Cancels a pending order with the given reason.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification of acceptable reason values. The clause requires a reason but fails to enumerate which reasons are valid, leaving the agent to decide acceptability without policy guidance. Per D004, the unambiguous version adds only the two enumerated values.

source_clause: After user confirmation, the total will be refunded via the original payment method.
ambiguous_version: After cancellation, the order total is refunded to the customer's payment method.
unambiguous_version: After cancellation, the order total is refunded to the original payment method used for the order. If the original payment method was a gift card, the refund is processed immediately. For all other payment methods, the refund is processed in 5 to 7 business days.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify refund timing, leaving the agent unable to inform customers when to expect funds.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The refund is immediate for all payment methods.
Interpretation B: The refund takes several business days for all payment methods.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent tells a credit card customer their refund is immediate. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly states 5–7 business days for credit card/PayPal refunds while gift card refunds are immediate.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_pending_order(order_id: string, reason: string) — Cancels the order and initiates refund.
annotation_rationale: Missing refund timing specification. The clause states refunds go to the original payment method but omits the timeline. Per D004, the unambiguous version adds only the timing rule (immediate for gift cards, 5–7 days otherwise) without additional edge cases.

source_clause: The modify items action can only be called once.
ambiguous_version: Items in a pending order can be modified, but this action has limitations.
unambiguous_version: Items in a pending order can be modified, but the modify_pending_order_items tool can only be called once per order. After it is called, no further item modifications or cancellations are possible for that order.
ambiguity_point: The clause mentions limitations without specifying what they are — particularly the one-time limit and the consequence that the order can no longer be cancelled.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Modifications can be made multiple times with some unspecified cap.
Interpretation B: Exactly one modification call is permitted, after which neither modification nor cancellation is possible.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent allows a second modification attempt when a customer wants to change another item. Under Interpretation B the agent proactively warns the customer to specify all changes in a single call and declines any subsequent modification requests.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies items in a pending order. Can only be called once per order.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification of the one-time limit and its consequence. The unambiguous version adds only the one-call limit and the resulting prohibition on further modifications/cancellations — nothing more.

source_clause: The new payment method for an order modification must not be the same as the existing one.
ambiguous_version: The customer can update the payment method on a pending order to a different one from their account.
unambiguous_version: The customer can update the payment method on a pending order to a different payment method from their account. The new payment method must have a different payment method ID than the current one. If the new payment method is a gift card, its balance must be sufficient to cover the order total.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify the balance requirement when the new payment method is a gift card.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent accepts any gift card the customer provides as the new method without checking balance.
Interpretation B: The agent must verify the gift card has sufficient balance to cover the order total before accepting it as the new payment method.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent switches the payment to a nearly depleted gift card, causing a payment failure. Under Interpretation B the agent checks the gift card balance first and declines if insufficient.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_payment(order_id: string, payment_method_id: string) — Changes the payment method of a pending order.
annotation_rationale: Missing gift card balance check condition. The clause states the new method must differ from the old one but does not address the gift card balance requirement. Per D004, only the balance-check rule is added.

source_clause: For exchange of a delivered order, the same product type constraint applies.
ambiguous_version: Customers can exchange items in a delivered order for different ones.
unambiguous_version: Customers can exchange items in a delivered order for different items of the same product type. The exchanged items must be of the same product type as the originals (e.g., shirt for shirt). A payment method must be provided to handle any price difference between the original and new items.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify that a payment method must be provided to cover price differences in an exchange.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Exchanges are always equal-value — no payment is required or accepted.
Interpretation B: Exchanges may involve a price difference that must be paid or refunded via a specified payment method.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent processes an exchange without asking for a payment method, causing the tool call to fail when there is a price difference. Under Interpretation B the agent asks for a payment method before processing.
stripped_tool_desc: exchange_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Processes an item exchange. Requires a payment method for price differences.
annotation_rationale: Missing payment method requirement. The source clause mentions same-type constraint but omits the payment method requirement for price differences. Per D004, only this single missing element is added.

source_clause: You have to authenticate the user identity by locating their user id via email, or via name + zip code.
ambiguous_version: Agents must confirm who they are speaking with before taking any account actions.
unambiguous_version: Agents must confirm the user's identity by looking up their user ID via email or via their full name plus zip code before taking any account actions. This lookup must be performed even if the user provides their user ID directly.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify whether the lookup is required when the user already provides their user ID.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: If the user provides their user ID, no further lookup is needed — the agent can proceed directly.
Interpretation B: The email or name+zip lookup must be performed regardless of whether the user provides their ID.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A an agent skips the authentication step when a user says 'my user ID is user_123'. Under Interpretation B the agent performs the email or name+zip lookup in all cases.
stripped_tool_desc: find_user_id_by_email(email: string) — Finds user ID by email. find_user_id_by_name_zip(first_name: string, last_name: string, zip: string) — Finds user ID by name and zip.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification that the lookup is required even when the user provides their own ID. This gap leads to authentication bypass under a reasonable reading. Per D004, only the 'even when user provides ID' clause is added.

source_clause: You must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation before taking any action that updates the database.
ambiguous_version: Before updating the database, agents should review the requested changes with the customer.
unambiguous_version: Before updating the database, agents must explicitly list all details of the action (e.g., order ID, items, amounts, payment method) and receive an explicit 'yes' confirmation from the customer. A general 'ok' or continuation of the conversation does not count as confirmation.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify what counts as 'explicit confirmation' — whether 'ok', 'sure', 'go ahead' or only 'yes' satisfies the requirement.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Any affirmative response ('ok', 'sure', 'sounds good') counts as confirmation.
Interpretation B: Only an explicit 'yes' (or direct affirmative) after the agent lists details counts as confirmation.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent proceeds after the customer says 'ok cool' without explicitly saying 'yes'. Under Interpretation B the agent requests a clear 'yes' before proceeding.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_pending_order(order_id: string, reason: string) — Cancels an order. Should only be called after explicit confirmation.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification of what constitutes 'explicit confirmation'. The clause says confirmation is required but does not define what counts. Per D004, only the definition of confirmation (explicit yes) is added.

source_clause: You can only help one user per conversation.
ambiguous_version: Each conversation is limited to one customer's requests.
unambiguous_version: Each conversation is limited to one customer's requests. If a second person attempts to make a request during the same conversation, the agent must decline their request and explain that they can only assist the authenticated user in this session.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify what the agent should do when a second person attempts to use the same conversation.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent simply stops helping and ends the conversation.
Interpretation B: The agent declines the second person's request and explains the limitation, but continues the conversation if the original user resumes.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent abruptly terminates the session when a second user appears. Under Interpretation B the agent politely declines the second person and remains available to the authenticated user.
annotation_rationale: Missing procedure for handling multi-user attempts. The clause restricts to one user but does not specify the response when another user attempts to interject. Per D004, only the decline-and-explain response is added.

source_clause: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions.
ambiguous_version: Agents should escalate unresolvable requests to human support.
unambiguous_version: Agents should transfer the user to a human agent when the user's request falls outside the scope of the permitted retail operations (cancel, modify, return, exchange, information). The agent must not transfer for requests that are in scope, even if they are complex.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not define what 'cannot be handled within scope' means — agents must judge what is in-scope without criteria.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Any request the agent finds difficult or uncertain is out-of-scope and should be escalated.
Interpretation B: Only requests that are explicitly outside the listed operations (cancel, modify, return, exchange, info) are out-of-scope.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent transfers a complex but technically in-scope cancellation request because it is difficult. Under Interpretation B the agent handles all in-scope requests and only transfers genuinely out-of-scope ones.
stripped_tool_desc: transfer_to_human_agents(summary: string) — Transfers the conversation to human support.
annotation_rationale: Missing definition of 'within scope'. The clause uses 'cannot be handled' without specifying the scope boundary. Per D004, only the explicit scope list (cancel, modify, return, exchange, information) is added as the definition.

source_clause: Each item can be modified to an available new item of the same product but of different product option.
ambiguous_version: Customers may change items in their pending order to a different variant.
unambiguous_version: Customers may change items in their pending order to a different variant (option) of the same product, provided the new item is currently available in inventory. If the desired variant is out of stock, the agent cannot process the modification and should inform the customer.
ambiguity_point: The clause requires the new item to be 'available' but does not specify what the agent should do if it is not available.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: If the variant is unavailable, the agent improvises — offers an alternative product type, backorder, or any available substitute.
Interpretation B: If the variant is unavailable, the agent declines the modification and informs the customer.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent substitutes a different product type when the requested option is unavailable. Under Interpretation B the agent informs the customer that the modification cannot proceed and ends the modification attempt.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies pending order items.
annotation_rationale: Missing procedure for unavailable-item case. The clause requires availability but omits the agent's response when the item is not available. Per D004, only the decline-and-inform response is added.

source_clause: Flight can be cancelled if any of the following is true: booking made within 24 hours, airline cancelled the flight, business flight, or insurance covers the reason.
ambiguous_version: Agents can cancel a flight if the user meets one of the standard cancellation conditions.
unambiguous_version: Agents can cancel a flight if at least one of the following conditions is confirmed: (1) the booking was made within the last 24 hours, (2) the airline cancelled the specific flight, (3) all flights in the reservation are in the business cabin, or (4) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered. Agents must verify the applicable condition before calling the cancellation tool.
ambiguity_point: The clause references 'standard cancellation conditions' without enumerating them, leaving the agent to infer or recall conditions from elsewhere.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent applies whichever conditions it recalls or infers as 'standard' — potentially applying conditions not in policy.
Interpretation B: The agent applies exactly the four listed conditions.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent may cancel a flight for a customer who expresses severe financial hardship, treating this as a 'standard' reason. Under Interpretation B the agent declines because financial hardship is not one of the four conditions.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels the reservation. No eligibility check performed.
annotation_rationale: Missing enumeration of conditions. Referring to 'standard conditions' without listing them forces the agent to supply conditions from memory or inference. Per D004, only the four enumerated conditions are added.

source_clause: If any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed.
ambiguous_version: Agents cannot modify or cancel reservations for flights that have already departed.
unambiguous_version: Agents cannot modify or cancel reservations if any flight segment in the reservation has already been flown. In such cases, the agent must transfer the user to a human agent rather than simply declining.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify what the agent should do after determining a flight has been flown — deny and end, or escalate.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent simply tells the customer it cannot help and ends the conversation.
Interpretation B: The agent transfers the customer to a human agent for further assistance.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent says 'I cannot help with that' and closes the conversation, leaving the customer with no path forward. Under Interpretation B the agent transfers to a human agent as required.
stripped_tool_desc: transfer_to_human_agents(summary: string) — Transfers to a human agent.
annotation_rationale: Missing escalation procedure after determining the flight has been flown. The clause says the agent cannot help but does not specify the transfer requirement. Per D004, only the transfer instruction is added.

source_clause: Only compensate if the user is a silver/gold member, has travel insurance, or flies business.
ambiguous_version: Agents may offer compensation to eligible customers who complain about flight disruptions.
unambiguous_version: Agents may offer compensation to customers who complain about flight disruptions, provided the customer meets at least one eligibility condition: silver or gold membership, active travel insurance on the reservation, or business cabin booking. Regular-tier members without insurance flying economy or basic economy are not eligible.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify what happens when a customer complains but is ineligible — should the agent simply decline or explain the eligibility criteria?
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent offers compensation anyway to avoid conflict with an insistent customer.
Interpretation B: The agent declines and, if pressed, explains that the customer does not meet the eligibility criteria.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent issues a certificate to avoid argument. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly declines based on eligibility and explains the criteria if asked.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate.
annotation_rationale: Missing procedure for ineligible-customer scenario. The clause defines who is eligible but does not specify the response when an ineligible customer requests compensation. Per D004, only the decline response is added.

source_clause: The amount of compensation for a cancelled flight is $100 times the number of passengers.
ambiguous_version: Agents can offer a certificate for cancelled flights based on the number of passengers affected.
unambiguous_version: Agents can offer a certificate for cancelled flights. The certificate amount is $100 multiplied by the total number of passengers listed in the reservation, regardless of how many passengers were personally affected or complained.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify whether 'number of passengers' means all passengers in the reservation or only those who complained or were personally affected.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Affected passengers' means only those who explicitly complained or were on the cancelled flight.
Interpretation B: 'Number of passengers' means all passengers listed in the reservation.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent issues a $100 certificate when only one of three passengers complains, rather than $300 for all three. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly calculates $100 × total reservation passengers.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a certificate of the specified amount.
annotation_rationale: Missing clarification that 'number of passengers' refers to reservation total, not subset. Per D004, only this clarification is added without additional rules.

source_clause: Checked bag allowance depends on the booking user's membership tier and the cabin class.
ambiguous_version: The free baggage allowance is based on the passenger's membership and cabin.
unambiguous_version: The free baggage allowance is based on the booking user's membership tier and the cabin class booked, per the following table: regular/basic-economy=0, regular/economy=1, regular/business=2, silver/basic-economy=1, silver/economy=2, silver/business=3, gold/basic-economy=2, gold/economy=3, gold/business=4. Allowance is determined by the booking user's tier, not individual passenger tiers.
ambiguity_point: The clause references a lookup but does not provide the actual table, leaving the agent without values for any specific tier+cabin combination.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent guesses or estimates baggage allowances from general knowledge.
Interpretation B: The agent applies the precise tier×cabin table.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent tells a silver member in economy they get 1 free bag (incorrect — should be 2). Under Interpretation B the agent correctly applies 2 free bags for silver/economy.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_baggages(reservation_id: string, total_baggages: int, payment_method_id: string) — Updates baggage count on a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Missing baggage allowance table. The clause references membership and cabin as determinants but omits the 9-cell lookup table. Per D004, only the table itself is added.

source_clause: A reservation can include at most one travel certificate, one credit card, and three gift cards as payment.
ambiguous_version: Multiple payment methods can be combined for a single booking.
unambiguous_version: Multiple payment methods can be combined for a single booking, subject to the following limits: at most one travel certificate, at most one credit card, and at most three gift cards. Any combination within these limits is acceptable.
ambiguity_point: The clause allows combination but does not specify the limits on each payment type, making it impossible for the agent to enforce the constraints.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Any number of each payment type can be combined — two certificates and five gift cards are acceptable.
Interpretation B: Specific limits apply: 1 certificate, 1 credit card, 3 gift cards maximum.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent accepts a payment split across two certificates and four gift cards. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly enforces the per-type limits.
stripped_tool_desc: book_reservation(user_id: string, origin: string, destination: string, flight_type: string, cabin: string, flights: list, passengers: list, payment_methods: list, travel_insurance: bool, add_checked_baggages: int) — Books a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Missing enumeration of per-type payment limits. The unambiguous version adds only the three specific limits (1 certificate, 1 card, 3 gift cards) without additional rules.

source_clause: Basic economy cannot be modified once booked.
ambiguous_version: Passengers in restricted fare classes have limited modification options.
unambiguous_version: Passengers booked in the basic economy cabin cannot make any modifications to their reservation's flights. This restriction applies regardless of when the booking was made, the reason for modification, or the destination.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify whether exceptions exist (e.g., airline-initiated changes, medical emergencies) or whether 'limited' means zero or reduced options.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: 'Limited' means some modifications are still possible under certain circumstances — the agent looks for exceptions.
Interpretation B: No modifications whatsoever are permitted for basic economy — zero options.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent offers a basic economy passenger a date change if they claim a medical emergency. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly refuses all modifications and explains the basic economy restriction.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Updates reservation flights.
annotation_rationale: Missing clarification that 'cannot modify' means zero exceptions (within agent scope). Per D004, only the 'regardless of reason or timing' clause is added to eliminate the exception-seeking behavior.

source_clause: Confirm the facts before offering compensation; do not proactively offer compensation.
ambiguous_version: Agents should verify the situation before discussing compensation with a customer.
unambiguous_version: Agents should verify the situation before discussing compensation. Specifically, the agent must confirm: (1) whether the relevant flight was actually cancelled or delayed, and (2) the number of passengers on the affected flights. The agent must not bring up compensation unless the customer explicitly asks.
ambiguity_point: The clause says 'verify the situation' but does not specify which facts must be confirmed before compensation can be offered.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: Verification means a general understanding of the customer's complaint — no specific facts need to be checked.
Interpretation B: Two specific facts must be confirmed: flight status (cancelled/delayed) and passenger count.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent offers a certificate after the customer describes their experience without verifying the cancellation or passenger count. Under Interpretation B the agent explicitly confirms both facts before calculating and offering the certificate.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification of which facts must be verified. Per D004, only the two required verification facts (cancellation/delay status and passenger count) are added.

source_clause: The origin and destination of the trip cannot be changed when modifying a reservation.
ambiguous_version: Some aspects of a flight reservation cannot be changed after booking.
unambiguous_version: The following aspects of a flight reservation cannot be changed after booking via the modify tool: (1) the origin airport, (2) the destination airport, and (3) the trip type (one-way or round-trip). Flight dates, times, and specific flight numbers can be changed.
ambiguity_point: The clause says 'some aspects' without listing them, leaving the agent unable to determine which changes are permitted.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent refuses all modification attempts to avoid violating undisclosed restrictions.
Interpretation B: The agent allows all modifications that are not explicitly prohibited.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent refuses to change a flight date because 'some aspects cannot be changed' and uncertainty causes over-restriction. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly changes the date while blocking origin/destination/trip-type changes.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Updates flight segments.
annotation_rationale: Missing enumeration of non-changeable aspects. Per D004, only the three specific prohibited changes (origin, destination, trip type) are added.

source_clause: A reservation can include at most 5 passengers.
ambiguous_version: There is a passenger limit for flight bookings.
unambiguous_version: Each reservation can include at most 5 passengers. If a customer requests a booking for more than 5 passengers, the agent must decline and explain the limit. Booking multiple separate reservations for the same trip is not a workaround the agent should offer.
ambiguity_point: The clause states there is a limit but does not specify the limit value, nor what the agent should do when a request exceeds it.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent applies a limit based on general knowledge (perhaps 9, a common airline group limit).
Interpretation B: The agent applies the specific 5-passenger limit and declines requests exceeding it.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent books 7 passengers because '5' was not explicitly stated. Under Interpretation B the agent declines any booking request for 6 or more passengers.
stripped_tool_desc: book_reservation(user_id: string, origin: string, destination: string, flight_type: string, cabin: string, flights: list, passengers: list, payment_methods: list, travel_insurance: bool, add_checked_baggages: int) — Books a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification of the passenger limit value and the handling procedure. Per D004, only the limit value (5) and the decline response are added.

source_clause: Return delivered order: the refund will be to the original payment method or a gift card.
ambiguous_version: Customers may choose their preferred refund method when returning an item.
unambiguous_version: Customers may choose their preferred refund method when returning an item: either to the original payment method used for the order or to an existing gift card in their account. The agent must ask the customer which refund method they prefer before initiating the return.
ambiguity_point: The clause allows choice but does not specify that the agent must ask the customer for their preference before proceeding.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent automatically refunds to the original payment method unless the customer explicitly requests a gift card.
Interpretation B: The agent must actively offer both options and ask the customer to choose before initiating the return.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent proceeds with an original-method refund without mentioning the gift card option. Under Interpretation B the agent presents both options and waits for the customer's choice.
stripped_tool_desc: return_delivered_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Initiates a return with the specified refund destination.
annotation_rationale: Missing step requiring the agent to ask for refund preference. The clause mentions options exist but omits the agent's obligation to present them. Per D004, only the ask-for-preference step is added.

source_clause: Modify items: the user must provide a payment method to pay or receive the price difference.
ambiguous_version: A payment method is needed for item modifications that involve a price change.
unambiguous_version: A payment method is needed for item modifications that involve a price change. If the modified items are more expensive than the originals, the payment method will be charged the difference. If the modified items are less expensive, the difference will be refunded to the specified payment method.
ambiguity_point: The clause requires a payment method but does not specify how it is used when the new items are cheaper (refund direction) vs. more expensive (charge direction).
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The payment method is only for charging price increases — refunds always go to the original order payment method.
Interpretation B: The same payment method handles both charges (for increases) and refunds (for decreases).
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent accepts a gift card as payment for an upcharge but ignores it for refund routing. Under Interpretation B the agent consistently uses the specified method for both directions.
stripped_tool_desc: modify_pending_order_items(order_id: string, item_ids: list, new_item_ids: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies items and handles price difference via the specified payment method.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification of bidirectional payment method usage. The clause states a method is needed but does not clarify that it covers both charges and refunds. Per D004, only this bidirectional clarification is added.

source_clause: Authenticate the user identity before providing any account information.
ambiguous_version: Users must be identified before the agent accesses their records.
unambiguous_version: Users must be identified before the agent accesses their records. If the agent cannot locate the user's account via email or name+zip, the agent must inform the customer that no matching account was found and cannot proceed with the request.
ambiguity_point: The clause requires identification but does not specify what the agent should do if no matching account is found.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: If no account is found, the agent asks for more identifying information and keeps trying.
Interpretation B: If no account is found after the standard lookup, the agent informs the customer and ends the authentication attempt.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent tries increasingly creative lookups (phone number, order ID, etc.) that are outside the defined authentication methods. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly informs the customer that no account was found and cannot proceed.
stripped_tool_desc: find_user_id_by_email(email: string) — Finds user by email. find_user_id_by_name_zip(first_name: string, last_name: string, zip: string) — Finds user by name and zip.
annotation_rationale: Missing procedure for failed authentication lookup. Per D004, only the inform-and-stop response for no-match scenarios is added.

source_clause: You should not make up any information not provided by the user or the tools.
ambiguous_version: Agents should only use information available to them during the conversation.
unambiguous_version: Agents should only state information that was explicitly provided by the customer during the conversation or returned by one of the available tools. If the requested information is not available from these sources, the agent must tell the customer it does not have that information rather than estimating or inferring.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify what the agent should do when asked for information that is not available — whether to say so explicitly or attempt to infer.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent estimates or infers missing information from context rather than saying it is unavailable.
Interpretation B: The agent explicitly tells the customer the information is not available through its current tools.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent says 'Your order probably arrived Tuesday based on the shipping date' without looking it up. Under Interpretation B the agent says 'I don't have that specific delivery confirmation — please check your tracking email.'
stripped_tool_desc: get_order_details(order_id: string) — Returns available order information.
annotation_rationale: Missing response procedure for information gaps. The clause prohibits fabrication but does not specify the alternative (explicit acknowledgment of unavailability). Per D004, only the tell-customer response is added.

source_clause: The delayed flight compensation is $50 times the number of passengers if the user wants to change or cancel the reservation.
ambiguous_version: Agents may provide delay compensation after processing a flight change or cancellation.
unambiguous_version: Agents may provide delay compensation after processing a flight change or cancellation requested by the customer. The compensation is $50 per passenger in the reservation. The agent must process the change or cancellation first, then offer the certificate — not before.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify the ordering: whether compensation is offered before or after the change/cancellation is processed.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent offers the certificate first, then processes the flight change — compensation is an incentive to proceed.
Interpretation B: The agent processes the flight change first, then offers the certificate — compensation follows the action.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent offers a $150 certificate before changing the flights, which the customer may then accept and cancel the change request, receiving compensation without any modification occurring. Under Interpretation B the agent correctly processes the change first.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate. update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, payment_method_id: string) — Modifies reservation flights.
annotation_rationale: Missing ordering specification between the change action and the compensation offer. Per D004, only the sequence instruction (change first, then certificate) is added.

source_clause: Do not offer compensation for any reason other than cancelled or delayed flights.
ambiguous_version: Compensation is only available for specific flight-related issues.
unambiguous_version: Compensation certificates are only available for two specific situations: (1) flights in the reservation that were cancelled by the airline, and (2) flights in the reservation that were delayed, provided the customer wants to change or cancel as a result. Compensation is not available for other inconveniences such as gate changes, seat reassignments, or poor service.
ambiguity_point: The clause says 'specific issues' without naming them, leaving the agent to infer which issues qualify.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent compensates for any significant inconvenience including overbooking, seat changes, or equipment swaps.
Interpretation B: Only the two specifically defined situations (cancellation, delay-with-change-request) qualify.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent offers a certificate to a customer who complains about an involuntary seat downgrade. Under Interpretation B the agent declines and explains only cancellations and qualifying delays are compensable.
stripped_tool_desc: add_certificate(amount: float, user_id: string) — Issues a compensation certificate.
annotation_rationale: Missing enumeration of the two qualifying situations. Per D004, only the two specific scenarios (cancellation, delay+change-request) are named as the eligible situations.

source_clause: The booking was made within the last 24 hours — one of the four cancellation eligibility conditions.
ambiguous_version: Customers who recently booked can cancel without conditions.
unambiguous_version: Customers whose booking was made within the last 24 hours (measured from the booking creation timestamp to the current time) can cancel without meeting any of the other eligibility conditions. The agent must check the booking timestamp to confirm the 24-hour window has not elapsed.
ambiguity_point: The clause does not specify how '24 hours' is measured — from booking creation, from departure, or from some other event — and does not say the agent must verify the timestamp.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: '24 hours' is measured from the scheduled departure time — customers can cancel any time up to 24 hours before the flight.
Interpretation B: '24 hours' is measured from the booking creation timestamp — customers can only cancel within 24 hours of making the booking.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent cancels a week-old booking because the flight is tomorrow (within 24 hours of departure). Under Interpretation B the agent correctly refuses because the booking is older than 24 hours.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification of the 24-hour measurement baseline (booking creation vs. departure). Per D004, only the clarification that it is measured from booking creation and requires timestamp verification is added.

source_clause: The cabin must be consistent across all flights in the reservation when modifying.
ambiguous_version: All flights in a reservation modification must be in the same cabin class.
unambiguous_version: All flights in a reservation modification must be in the same cabin class. The target cabin class for all flights must be specified at the time of modification. If the customer requests different cabins for different legs, the agent must decline the modification.
ambiguity_point: The clause requires consistency but does not specify what happens when a customer requests mixed cabins, nor whether the agent must actively ask for the target cabin.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent defaults to the current cabin for all legs without asking, assuming consistency is maintained.
Interpretation B: The agent must actively ask what cabin the customer wants for all legs and decline if different cabins are requested.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent silently applies the current cabin to all modified legs without confirming with the customer. Under Interpretation B the agent explicitly confirms the cabin class and rejects mixed-cabin modifications.
stripped_tool_desc: update_reservation_flights(reservation_id: string, flights: list, cabin: string, payment_method_id: string) — Updates flight segments; cabin must be specified.
annotation_rationale: Missing procedure for handling mixed-cabin requests and the requirement to confirm target cabin. Per D004, only the decline-for-mixed-cabin and confirm-cabin steps are added.

source_clause: You should deny user requests that are against this policy.
ambiguous_version: Agents should not help with requests that violate the retail policy.
unambiguous_version: Agents should not execute requests that violate the retail policy. When declining, the agent should inform the customer that the request is not permitted under the current policy and offer to help with any in-scope requests instead.
ambiguity_point: The clause says agents should not help but does not specify what the agent should say or do when declining — whether to explain, redirect, or simply refuse.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent abruptly refuses with minimal explanation and awaits the next message.
Interpretation B: The agent explains the policy reason for the refusal and offers to assist with permissible requests.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent says 'I cannot do that' with no further context. Under Interpretation B the agent explains why the request is not permitted and proactively asks if there is anything else it can help with.
annotation_rationale: Missing communication guidance for policy-denial responses. Per D004, only the explain-and-redirect response pattern is added without additional edge cases.

source_clause: If the user has travel insurance and the reason for cancellation is covered by insurance, the flight can be cancelled.
ambiguous_version: Customers with travel insurance may cancel their flight if their reason is covered.
unambiguous_version: Customers with travel insurance may cancel their flight if their stated cancellation reason is covered by their insurance policy. The agent must ask the customer to confirm that their insurance specifically covers the stated reason; the agent cannot independently verify insurance coverage and must rely on the customer's confirmation.
ambiguity_point: The clause requires the reason to be 'covered' but does not specify how the agent verifies coverage — whether to check a system, ask the customer, or accept the claim at face value.
possible_interpretations: Interpretation A: The agent independently verifies insurance coverage through a tool or system check.
Interpretation B: The agent asks the customer to confirm their insurance covers the reason and relies on that confirmation.
expected_agent_behavior_diff: Under Interpretation A the agent attempts a system lookup for insurance details, finds no such tool, and either blocks the cancellation or improvises. Under Interpretation B the agent asks the customer to confirm coverage and proceeds on the basis of that confirmation.
stripped_tool_desc: cancel_reservation(reservation_id: string) — Cancels a reservation.
annotation_rationale: Missing specification of the coverage verification method. Per D004, only the ask-customer-to-confirm procedure is added, clarifying that agent relies on customer confirmation rather than independent verification.
